concept.name: MACD line
concept.definition: The core series of the MACD: the fast (default 12-period) EMA minus the slow (default 26-period) EMA of closing prices, oscillating around zero as the two averages converge and diverge.
concept.intuition: The spread between a fast and a slow average: positive and widening means upside momentum is building.
concept.mechanics: Computed each bar as EMA_12(C) - EMA_26(C); it crosses zero exactly when the two EMAs cross, and its distance from zero measures how far the averages have diverged.
concept.failure_modes: As an EMA spread it lags and whipsaws in trendless markets; absolute values are price-scale dependent and not comparable across securities (use the PPO for that).
concept.misconceptions: A falling MACD line is not the same as falling prices — the EMA spread can shrink while prices are still rising, reflecting decelerating momentum only.
concept.example: A 12-day EMA of 50 and a 26-day EMA of 48 give a MACD line of +2: the fast average sits 2 points above the slow one.
